title: Minimum Operations to Transform String
summary: Given a string s made of lowercase English letters, you can replace each character with the next letter in the alphabet any number of times.
statement: Given a string s made of lowercase English letters, you can replace each character with the next letter in the alphabet any number of times. Determine the least number of operations needed to convert the string entirely into 'a' characters, considering 'a' to be followed by 'z' in a circular manner.
constraints: In one operation, any chosen characters may advance one step in the cycle a→z→y→...→a defined by the source rule.
reference_solution:
def minimum_cyclic_letter_operations(s):
    return max([0]+[26-(ord(c)-ord('a')) for c in s if c!='a'])
hints: Each non-a letter has a fixed remaining distance 26-index from a.
Characters may advance together, so the total time is the maximum individual distance.
Ignore letters already at a and take the maximum, defaulting to zero.
A shorter schedule cannot finish the farthest letter, and advancing every unfinished letter attains the maximum.
editorial: A shorter schedule cannot finish the farthest letter, and advancing every unfinished letter attains the maximum.

tests.explanation: Both characters can reach a within two synchronized steps.
